page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, supplying 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without hyperthreading (1 thread per core). Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 128 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration stands at 128.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local physical storage is directly integrated, featuring an 1888 GB NVMe SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier memory subsystems and strong multithreaded compute throughput. While single-core evaluations register within average ranges—achieving 2073.49 in stress-ng single-core and 1686.0 in Geekbench single-core—parallel workloads perform competitively. In multi-core tests, the server logged a stress-ng result of 66288.64 and a Geekbench score of 20037.0, supported by software compilation metrics reaching 39783.0. Uncached memory throughput ranks in the top tier, measuring 448.6 GB/sec for large block reads and 188.32 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations also achieved top-tier placement at 37354.99 points.

Cost efficiency is highlighted by high compute density and local disk integration, providing large NVMe scratch storage and solid memory bandwidth without requiring auxiliary drives for temporary storage. Tradeoffs stem from the ARM64 ISA, which lacks x86 vector extensions (AVX, AVX-512, AMX), and limited capability for heavy floating-point or large-scale AI pipelines. LLM inference processing degrades sharply with larger models, evidenced by a 4.65 tokens/sec rate for 70B prompt processing. Consequently, the D32pds_v6 is structurally suited for multi-threaded build systems, database engines, data caching tiers, and static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose ARM64 virtual machine featuring a 32-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores. Configured with 128.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) and an integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD local drive, this server delivers balanced system resources without a dedicated GPU. Performance metrics highlight top-tier memory bandwidth, with large-block reads reaching 448.6 GB/sec and writes at 188.32 GB/sec, alongside top-tier PassMark database operations scores. Multi-core performance is robust across stress-ng and Clang compilation benchmarks, although single-core execution remains average and heavy AI workloads are limited by the absence of vector acceleration. The server fits database hosting, CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-volume web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
